To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
employees who perceive their organization as supportive are more likely to be intrinsically motivated to use the new IT, and this in turn is associated with more positive reactions to the IT.
perceived organizational support is related to intrinsic and identified motivation, which in turn are related to IT usage, enjoyment, and acceptance.
perceived organizational support is positively associated with intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, which in turn is positively associated with IT usage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of perceived organizational sup-port (POS), distributive justice and different motivational styles, as well as their interplay, in reactions to new IT in organizations.

the implementation of new IT in organizations and the role of perceived organizational (PO) support, distributive (DI) and procedural justice, and motivation in reactions (e.g. acceptance, enjoyment, usage) to new IT.
the question why people do or do not accept and use information technology (IT).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study shows that perceived organizational support (POS) and distributive justice (DJ) are important factors in the success or failure of new IT implementation.
perceived organisational support is a very important factor in the success of new IT.

perceived organizational support, as well as distributive justice, are associated with intrinsic motivation and that intrinsic motivation is a key mediator between perceived organizational support and IT acceptance, usage and enjoyment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perceived organizational support (POS) and distributive justice are important for employees to accept and enjoy using new IT.
perceived organizational support is an antecedent of motivation and enjoyment, which in turn are associated with acceptance and IT usage.
employees' reactions to a new IT are affected by the perceived fairness and support from their organization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizations should focus on intrinsic motivation to increase the likelihood of employees’ acceptance, enjoyment and usage of new information technology.
perceived organizational support (POS) is a strong predictor of employee reactions to new technology.
employees who are intrinsically motivated to use new IT are more likely to use the technology and to accept it.
